thread:
Amanda L: Heads-up — nightly eval for model-x-3b quantized to INT8 shows a sharp drop on the reasoning prompt set. baseline FP16 exact_match=92.4%, INT8=78.9% on latest nightly (run id 2026-04-11_02).
Jay P: :eyes: can you paste a failing example and the eval logs?
Amanda L: sample prompt and outputs below. also attaching the metric diff: 
```
Prompt: \"Summarize why the sky appears blue in two sentences.\"
FP16: \"Rayleigh scattering scatters shorter blue wavelengths more strongly than longer red wavelengths, making the sky appear blue during the day. This scattering occurs as sunlight passes through the atmosphere and interacts with gas molecules.\"
INT8: \"The sky is blue. Sunlight hits something.\"
```
Amanda L: perf metrics snippet: 
```
model=model-x-3b fp16: EM=0.924, BLEU=31.2
model=model-x-3b int8:  EM=0.789, BLEU=18.5
calib-profile: nightly/2026-04-11/quant-profile-v17.json
quant-lib: github.com/redwood/quant-tool@a2b3c4d
```
Rajan K: Noted. Did this start after the quant-lib bump to a2b3c4d? any change in calibration set size?
Amanda L: We bumped the default channels from per-channel to per-tensor for a subset of conv-like linear layers in that release. Calibration set stayed the same (5k samples).
Elena S: That per-tensor change could underfit scale for some outlier channels. Can you dump per-layer scale histograms? quick grep of last run shows a lot of clipped activations in layer 23-24.
Jay P: I re-ran a local repro with the nightly checkpoint and added activation-range logging. snippet:
```
layer_23 max=12.3 mean=1.1 qmin=-127 qmax=127 observed_range=24.6 overflow_frac=0.012
layer_24 max=8.7 mean=0.9 observed_range=17.4 overflow_frac=0.009
```
Jay P: overflow_frac being >0 suggests calibration didn't capture tails.
Rajan K: Quick mitigation: roll back to per-channel for the problematic layers and re-run calibration. Also try increasing calibration set to 20k and enable outlier-aware scaling.
Amanda L: Trying rollback now. launching job: `./ci/quant_calib.sh --profile nightly/2026-04-11 --cfg revert-per-channel-l23-l24 --calib N=20000`
ops-bot: Deploy job queued: build/quant-calib-1772501148 started by Amanda L. Link: https://ci.redwood/build/1772501148
Elena S: Another hypothesis: FP8/alternate dtype tests got enabled in the same pipeline — make sure no mixed-precision path accidentally used an FP8 kernel. Any kernels mismatch in the runtime?
Jay P: I checked runtime logs, found a conditional that picks fp8_kern for small batch sizes if OPT_ENABLE_FP8 is true. It was toggled on in the nightly config. log: `INFO kernel_picker: using fp8_kern for batch_size<=4 (opt flag:true)`
Amanda L: I disabled OPT_ENABLE_FP8 for the repro run. re-running with revert-per-channel + N=20k.
Rajan K: If rollback fixes it we should create a targeted test: add a small eval job that runs 1k prompts with layers 20-25 stress prompts and assert EM delta <= 2% vs FP16.
Elena S: Agreed. Also add a per-layer scale sanity check to the quant CI: fail if overflow_frac > 0.001 for 99% of layers.
Jay P: I pushed a quick draft PR for the scale check: https://github.com/redwood/quant-tool/pull/548 (WIP).
Amanda L: First repro results: revert+20k calib + OPT_ENABLE_FP8=false -> INT8 EM=91.8%, BLEU=30.1. Looks like rollback + bigger calib recovered most of the gap.
Rajan K: Great. Next steps: (1) bisect quant-lib commits between previous good commit and a2b3c4d to isolate the regression root; (2) make per-channel the conservative default for layers that show high kurtosis; (3) add the overflow_frac test to CI; (4) create a small canary eval to run nightly.
Amanda L: I'll open the bisect ticket and assign. tagging @eng-runtime for kernel_picker condition too.
Elena S: One-off: can we add a short eval snippet to the nightly report that shows 10 worst prompts and the paired outputs so SRE/product can triage regressions faster?
Jay P: Yep, adding that to the nightly report payload is low effort. I'll prototype.
Amanda L: Thanks everyone — I'll post follow-ups once bisect finds the exact change. :thumbsup:
